about: The self-cleanup registry: the one list of what counts as trash, who sweeps it, and when. sweep.js (browser), magi/sweep.py (MAGI engine) and tests/cleanup-rules.test.js all read this file. An item deletes only when its 'delete' is true; false means dry run (listed in the sweep report, nothing removed). A new item ships false until Tony has seen its report. Add an item whenever a feature is removed. When in doubt, keep: an item needs an owner, a reason and a cap.

handledElsewhere: KV caches, tokens and locks that expire on their own (expirationTtl): newshub-api (meta, quota_block, stage:*, cal, summary, quotes, locks), WX_CACHE, PV_CACHE, oi:state, oi:toks, oi:sched, gat/pw_gat/oi:gat/kroger_tok, reset:, fail:, wb_account, tesla labels
workers2/taskhub-weather-api and workers2/proview-api: one-time sweeps of legacy TTL-less keys, already run
A1_BACKUPS objects: the index-backups GC, which must keep failing closed (memory index-backups-object-gc)
MAGI Code Mode sandboxes: magi/code/sandbox.py sweep() at startup
MAGI artifacts over 200 files: BrowserProvider._prune_artifacts after each save
MAGI upload folders: removed with their run or brainstorm session
index.html _freeWebStorage and riftiq WR_EVICTABLE: quota relief for regenerable caches when localStorage is full
never: anything tracked in git (plans, handoff docs, notes)
A1Backup and its objects (Index Backups/, A1_BACKUPS)
TradeHub journal snapshots (IndexedDB and their Firestore doc)
trashed-but-restorable items inside their own 30-day TTL
user data even when corrupt: journal entries, TaskHub, vault items, magi.db, uploads (log it and show Tony)
journal entry locks (jlock:*): hashes for entries that may still exist
